JGc_1,12.2 // [Sragdharā] [5] And then, once upon a time, the illustrious Queen of Vraja, the wife of the glorious Abhinanda, arrived at the assembly hall in the morning; becoming intent on her inquiry, she asked her: "O Mother of Kṛṣṇa, where has your son gone this very morning?"
[6] But the Queen of Vraja said with a smile: "Alas!
Until this present moment, I have been performing for him the tasks of massaging his body, bathing him, and dressing him.
Now, causing even me embarrassment, he—who is so dear to his own companions and servants—comes toward me at this time having performed those very rites separately."

Having arrived, he daily honors my father and the other elders with salutations and profound respect, according to their respective ranks. Furthermore, from that time on, whenever my calf returns at twilight while I am meditating upon his arrival,

But now,
by him who increases his efforts with oaths while seeking to refute that [position], my hands are rendered helpless;

And as that dark-complexioned youth departed, the cows followed him, walking very slowly as if they were gazing intently at the tips of his calves. Thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, having with great difficulty turned back those people who were longing to follow them on the path, and having liberated themselves from the fetters of their eyes, [departed].
Together with their friends, who were all adorned with graceful ornaments and surrounded by the great splendor of the young cowherds,

they suddenly laughed and shone as they moved toward the direction of Govardhana with a graceful gait; from time to time, they would stop so that all the cows might rest, having already satisfied their own hearts' desires.

but they were not shattered by being struck with sticks.
And there, as the female friends adorned one another together with them, and as they delighted and produced playfulness, a supreme curiosity manifested itself.
[38] Having observed this, the gods described it as follows:

"Each of these cows is externally the very form of the life-breath (prāṇa) of Hari; for when they are eternally satisfied, He attains satisfaction, and when they suffer from hunger, He experiences the affliction of hunger."

Bringing them one by one to his own heart, providing them with the pleasure of scent, embracing them, smelling them intensely, gathering them, offering them food, and protecting them, he shines by means of himself.

for in the Padma Purāṇa, a clear statement is seen regarding the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kārttika as the day on which the beginning of tending the cattle occurred.
The month of Bhādrapada alone is the time when the palmyra fruit ripens, and it is during that month that the shaking of the Dhenuka tree is well known;
therefore, we shall first propagate the subduing of Kāliya.

Turning back again and again to gaze at him, experiencing an intensifying anguish, and with great difficulty making their way toward home, they entered the interior of the palace while proclaiming the widespread fame of the glory of their lineage, which was foremost among their own kin. However—
